Hi all — technical answers below, pulling from hosting and runtime behavior: 

- Training on customer data: Hosted API telemetry/logging is used for quality monitoring and debugging only; we do NOT use customer prompts/responses to retrain or fine-tune models that are part of the shared Redwood model catalog. When customers opt-in to an explicit research program we document scope and obtain approvals. (We can provide a legal attestation for this.)

- Default retention: Raw prompt/response text is retained for 30 days in the hosted stack by default, then moved to a 90‑day analytics store where strings are hashed/pseudonymized. Embeddings and aggregated metrics are retained for 365 days by default. Those windows are configurable per-account and can be shortened on request.

- Opt-out controls: The hosted API has an account-level flag (data_processing.opt_out_training = true) that disables retention of raw text beyond immediate processing; when enabled, we only keep minimal routing metadata for 7 days for debugging. Dedicated/Private customers manage their own retention entirely.

- Deletion/erasure process:
  1) Customer requests deletion via the Console or support ticket.
  2) We enqueue a deletion job that zeroes the primary datastore objects and issues a downstream invalidation message to replication/analytics pipelines.
  3) Backups are rotated and marked; we run a targeted re-encryption/overwrite for affected segments and record an audit entry.
  4) We produce a deletion certificate (signed by Engineering + Compliance) listing object IDs and timestamps.

- Exports and evidence: We can produce redacted logs (PII masked) and the audit certificate. ETA: redacted logs + deletion certificate in 3 business days, CAIQ mapping within 2 business days. I've attached a redacted sample (stub) and an internal runbook.

Let me know if FinHealth needs the deletion certificate notarized or extended logging.

Thanks,
